core_obligations: At the generic point eta of the integral scheme, identify the restriction of E in D(kappa(eta)) with a finite complex V^bullet of finite dimensional vector spaces with zero differentials, and set r_i = dim V^i (proof lines 13117-13120).

Construct the perfect object E' represented by the complex with terms O_X^{r_i} and zero differentials, note that it becomes isomorphic to E after pulling back to eta, and conclude by relative perfectness descent that E and E' agree on an open neighbourhood U of eta, so that H^i(E|_U) is finite locally free of constant rank r_i (proof lines 13121-13127).

Deduce the blowup assertion from the first part and the blowup lemma, using that a nonempty open is scheme theoretically dense in the integral scheme X so that a U-admissible blowup is available (proof lines 13127-13129).
proof_roadmap: Read off the ranks at the generic point and build the model complex (proof lines 13117-13123).
Spread the model out to an open neighbourhood by relative perfectness descent (proof lines 13124-13127).
Get the blowup from the earlier blowup lemma (proof lines 13127-13129).
difficulty_reason: For a perfect complex E on an integral scheme X the lemma produces a nonempty open U on which every cohomology sheaf H^i(E|_U) is finite locally free of constant rank r_i, together with a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X such that every H^i(Lb^*E) is perfect of tor dimension at most one (statement lines 13105-13113). The proof of the existence of U is genuinely written out despite the author's rhetorical remark: at the generic point eta the complex E becomes a finite complex of finite dimensional vector spaces with zero differentials, with dimensions r_i; the perfect object E' represented by the complex with terms O_X^{r_i} and zero differentials becomes isomorphic to E after pulling back to eta, and the relatively perfect descent lemma then gives an open neighbourhood U of eta on which E and E' agree (proof lines 13116-13127). The blowup assertion is then deduced from the first part and the earlier blowup lemma, using that any nonempty open is scheme theoretically dense in an integral scheme (proof lines 13127-13129). Building the model complex from the dimensions at the generic point and applying relative perfectness to spread it out is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
